findings.issue: Standalone sentence-final 何 (no copula after it) is read なに, not なん; なん occurs only before だ/です/の, counters, and t/d/n sounds. Casual あれ何？ is read あれなに？ (cf. これ、何？ = これ、なに in standard textbook dialogues).
何 with no following copula/counter is なに in this casual question; なん is the pre-だ/です/の/counter variant (as correctly used in the sibling sentence あれは何ですか).
Romaji follows the wrong kana reading of 何; with the correct reading なに it should be arenani.
The same natural sentence is duplicated twice (copy-paste defect). The part before the parentheses should be the hyper-literal structural mirror, as lit_pt does ('Muito sair-querer-não-era').
findings.current: I didn't really want to go out. (I didn't really want to go out.)
findings.suggested: Not-really go-out-want-not-was. (I didn't really want to go out.)

findings.issue: 'does she get it?' misrenders 区別が付く: 'she' is a calque of the Portuguese feminine pronoun in lit_pt ('ela' = a distinção) and suggests a female person; 'get it' reads as 'understand'. English needs 'it' plus a 'take hold / be made' sense of 付く.
findings.current: As for the distinction between duck and goose, does she get it?
findings.suggested: As for the distinction between duck and goose, does it 'take' (can it be made)?

findings.issue: Drops も ('too/also'), which both pt ('também') and lit_en ('That man too...') keep; the additive nuance that this man, like others, is finished is part of the meaning.
findings.suggested: That guy is done for, too.

findings.issue: expl_en and expl_pt claim this かかる is 'a different sense' from the TIME/PRICE かかる. It is the same 'resources required' sense (時間・金・手間・手がかかる all fall under it in dictionaries), merely lexicalized as an idiom; the token gloss itself says 'to require / to take', contradicting the explanation.
findings.current: this is not the かかる of TIME/PRICE; here it is part of the fixed expression 手がかかる ('to be a handful'), a different sense
findings.suggested: it is the same 'takes/requires (time, money, effort)' sense of かかる, lexicalized in the idiom 手がかかる ('to require much care')

findings.issue: lit_en does not mirror the 手が + かかる structure the way lit_pt does ('mão (=trabalho) toma'); it just repeats the natural translation, so the English literal field gives no structural help.
findings.current: As for that child, he's a handful.
findings.suggested: As for that child, the hand (=care/effort) 'takes' (is required).
